questions.q: Explain how the Java Virtual Machine makes compiled Java programs platform independent.
questions.model: javac compiles source to platform-neutral bytecode (.class). Each platform has its own JVM that loads, verifies and interprets/JIT-compiles the bytecode, so the same .class file runs anywhere a JVM exists.

questions.q: What does this code print? String s1 = "java"; String s2 = new String("java"); System.out.println((s1 == s2) + " " + s1.equals(s2));
questions.model: == compares references (s2 is a new object), equals() compares contents: false true.

questions.q: A program calls sc.nextInt() to read an age and then sc.nextLine() to read a name, but the name is always empty. Explain the cause and give a fix.
questions.model: nextInt() reads the number but leaves the newline in the buffer; the next nextLine() returns that empty remainder. Fix: call sc.nextLine() once after nextInt() to consume the newline, or read the age with Integer.parseInt(sc.nextLine()).

questions.q: Write a Java class BankAccount with fields accountNumber and balance, a no-argument constructor that sets balance to 0, an overloaded constructor taking both values, and methods deposit() and withdraw() that reject invalid amounts.
In Java, the automatic conversion of an int into an Integer object is called ___, and the conversion of an Integer back to int is called ___.
questions.model: Autoboxing and unboxing.

questions.q: Which of the following is resolved at run time in Java?
questions.model: Overriding is dynamic dispatch, chosen by the object's run-time class; overloading is resolved at compile time.

questions.q: Read the assertion and reason about abstract and final classes and choose the correct option.
questions.assertion: An abstract class cannot be instantiated.
questions.reason: An abstract class must declare at least one abstract method.
questions.model: A is true. R is false: a class can be declared abstract with no abstract methods.

questions.q: Define an interface Shape with a method double area(). Implement it in classes Circle and Rectangle, and write main() that stores both in a Shape[] array and prints the total area.

Explain the visibility of private, default (package), protected and public members to: the same class, another class in the same package, a subclass in another package, and an unrelated class in another package.
questions.model: private: same class only. default: same class and same package. protected: same package plus subclasses in other packages. public: everywhere.

questions.q: Which of the following is a checked exception in Java?
questions.model: IOException must be caught or declared; the others are RuntimeException subclasses (unchecked).

questions.q: Define a checked exception InsufficientBalanceException. Write a method withdraw(double amount) that throws it when the balance is too low, and show a caller that handles it with try-catch-finally.
Design a bounded buffer of capacity 5 shared by a producer thread and a consumer thread using synchronized methods with wait() and notifyAll(). Explain why the condition is checked in a while loop.
questions.model: class Buffer { Queue<Integer> q = new LinkedList<>(); synchronized void put(int x) throws InterruptedException { while (q.size() == 5) wait(); q.add(x); notifyAll(); } synchronized int take() throws InterruptedException { while (q.isEmpty()) wait(); int x = q.remove(); notifyAll(); return x; } }. A while loop re-checks the condition after waking because of spurious wake-ups and because another thread may have changed the state first.

questions.q: Distinguish byte streams from character streams in Java and state which you would use to copy an image file and to read a text file containing Hindi text.
questions.model: Byte streams (InputStream/OutputStream) move raw 8-bit bytes; character streams (Reader/Writer) handle 16-bit characters with encoding. Image: FileInputStream/FileOutputStream. Hindi text: a Reader with the right charset (e.g. InputStreamReader with UTF-8).

questions.q: Compare a raw List with List<String>: what error does each one catch, and when, if an Integer is added and later cast to String?
questions.model: With a raw List the add compiles and the cast fails at run time with ClassCastException. List<String> rejects the add at compile time, so the error is found earlier and no cast is needed (type safety).

questions.t: ArrayList, LinkedList HashSet and ArrayDeque classes
questions.q: What does this print? Set<String> s = new HashSet<>(List.of("a", "b", "a", "c", "b")); System.out.println(s.size());
questions.model: A HashSet keeps distinct elements: a, b, c, so the size is 3.

questions.t: ArrayList, LinkedList HashSet and ArrayDeque classes
questions.q: For each requirement in the case, choose ArrayList, LinkedList, HashSet or ArrayDeque and justify your choice using the time complexity of the operations involved.
questions.case: A library system must (1) keep the catalogue so that books can be shown by position on a page, (2) record unique member IDs and check membership quickly, and (3) hold book-return requests that are processed strictly in arrival order, with frequent additions at the end and removals from the front.
questions.model: (1) ArrayList: O(1) indexed access. (2) HashSet: average O(1) add and contains, no duplicates. (3) ArrayDeque used as a queue: O(1) addLast and pollFirst without LinkedList's per-node overhead.

questions.q: State three advantages of Swing components over AWT components.
questions.model: Swing components are lightweight (drawn in Java, not by native peers), have a pluggable look and feel, and offer richer controls such as JTable and JTree; they behave consistently across platforms.

questions.q: Explain the event delegation model in Java using a JButton click as an example, naming the source, the event object and the listener.
questions.model: The JButton (source) generates an ActionEvent when clicked and delivers it to the objects registered with addActionListener(); each listener implements ActionListener.actionPerformed(ActionEvent). Handling is delegated to the listeners.

questions.q: Which JDBC driver type is written entirely in Java and converts JDBC calls directly into the database's network protocol?
questions.model: The Type 4 (thin) driver is pure Java and speaks the database protocol directly.

questions.q: Write Java code using JDBC that inserts a student (roll, name) into a table STUDENT with a PreparedStatement and then prints all rows. Explain why PreparedStatement is safer than building the SQL string by concatenation.
